page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz with 1 thread per core, providing 8 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 32 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It contains no local NVMe storage and does not include any GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across multi-core and memory operations. The instance achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 14472.4 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6000.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 563.91 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 87.42 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is weaker, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1073.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 6205.54, both falling into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Cryptographic performance is also limited, as shown by a weak Passmark CPU encryption score of 1300.22, despite hardware-level AES support.

The t2a-standard-8 exhibits significant performance degradation in LLM inference tasks, with text generation on a small 135M model scoring in the bottom 10% at 32.29 tokens/sec. It is also weak in single-threaded decompression and image processing. Conversely, it demonstrates stable throughput for static web serving at 10.09 GB/sec and handles Redis SET operations at 10.91 million operations per second. This profile makes the instance suitable for scale-out general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from dedicated physical cores, while it is poorly suited for machine learning inference or heavy cryptographic tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an ARM-based general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated physical cores on an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It is configured with 32 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, with no local storage or GPU acceleration. Benchmark results place its multi-core performance and memory bandwidth in the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6000.0 and static web serving throughput of 10.09 GB/sec. However, single-core capabilities and cryptographic execution are weak, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 6205.54 and a low LLM text generation speed of 32.29 tokens/sec. This instance is suited for scale-out workloads, static web serving, and database operations, offering a balanced resource profile with dedicated physical cores, though it is not recommended for compute-intensive single-threaded tasks or machine learning inference.
